title: Video editing: the user's own footage
description: Editing footage the user supplies into a finished video: a podcast episode or clips from it, a talking-head video for YouTube, Shorts, TikTok, Reels or LinkedIn, a trailer or teaser cut from existing shots, a founder-and-product launch cut, or a fast Gen Z social edit. ffmpeg does the editorial (probe, transcript, paper edit, cut list, reframe, audio cleanup, conform), the project layers captions, titles, b-roll, zooms and the end card on top, and every cut, caption and loudness figure is measured before delivery.
summary: Footage in, finished edit out: transcript, paper edit, ffmpeg cut and conform, captions and graphics on top, measured loudness.

requires.why: Probe, cut, reframe, clean the audio, conform the edit and measure the export. The editorial lives here.
Word timestamps drive the paper edit, filler removal and word-timed captions.
Bring the user's footage, music and b-roll into assets/.
The edit's dialogue, the music bed and every sound effect go on the timeline.
Check footage frames, caption placement and safe zones at every cut.
Every scene that layers graphics over the footage must load.
A bed for clips, trailers and launch cuts, legally sourced.
Pops, dings and hits on captions, key numbers and title cards.

route.deliverable: A finished edit of footage the user supplies: podcast episode or clips, talking-head video, trailer, launch cut or social edit
askFirst: Where will it be posted (YouTube, TikTok/Reels/Shorts, LinkedIn, a podcast feed), so I know the aspect and length?
How long should the finished edit be, or how many clips do you want from it?
Which style: clean and professional, or fast and native to TikTok?

models.note: Instrumental bed at an exact length; ask for a whole-frame BPM if you will cut to it.
Pop, ding, hit, tonal riser. Describe the sound, not the picture.
